name: Isenathi

hero.alt: Isenathi and her mom laughing together on the hillside at home

headline: When Isenathi first came to Siyakwazi, she couldn't crawl.

before_slider.p: She is almost five and lives with cerebral palsy. Our therapists started with the basics: sitting, then crawling. Within months she was pulling herself up to stand. Then she was walking with a little trolley. Then she didn't need the trolley.

before_slider.quote: "Her gross motor skills developed the fastest," says her therapist. "But the biggest change in Isenathi is her social communication. She's so bubbly and bright, talks so beautifully, and engages with people."

slides.alt: Isenathi with her schoolmates at the crèche
Isenathi's practitioner with her hands on Isenathi's shoulders at the crèche
slides.caption: "In any activity I include her. She is in the group of others."

slides.alt: Isenathi on the swing in the crèche playground
slides.note: The practitioner describes her climbing the ladder and riding the swing on her own (isiZulu)

slides.alt: Isenathi writing with a blue crayon
Isenathi writing at the table at home
Isenathi and her mom laughing together
Isenathi's family at home: her uncle, gogo, mom, Isenathi and another uncle
slides.caption: "My family is a very supportive family."

slides.alt: Isenathi laughing on the couch with her gogo and her mom
slides.caption: "They support me through my journey with Isenathi, because it was not, it was so difficult, but it was easy because I get some support from them."

slides.alt: Isenathi drawing at the table with her mom
slides.caption: "Her mom and her gogo ... have made sure that Isenathi knows ... all her body parts and basic concepts, and really laid a really great foundation for her when she starts to go to school."

slides.alt: Chicks under a heat lamp, part of Isenathi's mom's business
slides.caption: "I'm a businesswoman. I sell chickens."

slides.alt: Isenathi close up, smiling, her hand on her head
slides.caption: "She's blossomed."

after_slider.p: That didn't happen by accident. Her mom, her uncle and her gogo came to every session. Her mom joined our parent support group. Her uncle joined the Siyakwazi sewing hub, where he makes learning resources for other children and earns an income for the household. Isenathi started creche this year, and her practitioners give her the classroom support she needs to keep up.

after_slider.display: One child. A whole family lifted.

after_slider.p: As US aid pulls back, the gap for families like hers keeps growing. Siyakwazi is still here because you are. Your gift pays for the therapy, the parent support and the classroom help that turned a child who couldn't crawl into a confident little girl ready for school.
after_slider.flag: Team flag: "Your gift pays for the therapy" implies a gift designated to Siyakwazi (per-partner giving was removed 2026-10-13).

after_slider.lead: There are more children like Isenathi waiting for their first session.

intro.lead: This year, a lot of the help that reached South African families disappeared. Here's what your support kept going.
